en: Itivuttaka 43 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. This discourse was spoken by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, concerning two bhikkhus who were formerly brahmins. Having heard this, the bhikkhus asked the Blessed One about its meaning. “Bhikkhus, what is the cause, what is the reason, why these two bhikkhus who were formerly brahmins dwell with such great mutual affection? “Venerable sir, when we were novices, we studied under the same teacher. We were well-versed in the hymns, having mastered the Three Vedas, together with their vocabularies, ritual manuals, phonology, and etymology, as well as the histories as a fifth; we were skilled in philology and grammar, and we could even refute in debate those who opposed us. Yet, venerable sir, we do not recall ever seeing such great mutual affection among them as we see between these two bhikkhus who were formerly brahmins. “Bhikkhus, these two bhikkhus who were formerly brahmins were dear and beloved to one another. When they lived the household life, they would eat from the same vessel, drink from the same vessel, and share the same seat. Even after they had gone forth, they continued to live with such great mutual affection. Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has taken a loan from another, and that debt remains unpaid. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has lent a loan to another, and that debt remains outstanding. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has renounced the training and returned to the lower life. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has renounced the training and returned to the lower life, yet he still owes a debt to the Noble Ones. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, yet he does not train in accordance with the training. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and he trains in accordance with the training. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and though he trains in accordance with the training, he falls away from the higher virtue. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and though he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, he does not attain the higher mind. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, and he attains the higher mind. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and though he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, and attains the higher mind, he does not realize the higher wisdom. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, and attains the higher mind, and realizes the higher wisdom. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. Of these two, bhikkhus, which person is the superior, the more excellent, the more sublime, the more distinguished? “It is the person who is a creditor, venerable sir. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What are the two? The person who is a debtor and the person who is a creditor. These two persons, bhikkhus, are found existing in the world. What, bhikkhus, is the person who is a debtor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and though he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, and attains the higher mind, and realizes the higher wisdom, he does not become one who has reached the end of the spiritual journey, one who has done what was to be done, one who has laid down the burden, one who has attained his own goal, one whose fetters of existence are destroyed, and one who is liberated through final knowledge. This, bhikkhus, is called the person who is a debtor. And what, bhikkhus, is the person who is a creditor? Here, bhikkhus, someone has been ordained in this Dhamma and Discipline, and he trains in accordance with the training and does not fall away from the higher virtue, and attains the higher mind, and realizes the higher wisdom, and becomes one who has reached the end of the spiritual journey, one who has done what was to be done, one who has laid down the burden, one who has attained his own goal, one whose fetters of existence are destroyed, and
The Discourse on the Unborn.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, there is an unborn, an unbecome, an unmade, an unconditioned."
“Bhikkhus, if this unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned were not, an escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned would not be discerned here.
But because, bhikkhus, there is an unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned, therefore an escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned is discerned.
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
In this regard, it is said:
"That which is born, become, arisen, made, conditioned, and unstable;"
A conflagration of old age and death,
a nest of disease, fragile,
and originating from the conduit of nutriment.
It is not fit to delight in that;
its escape is peaceful,
beyond the sphere of logic, and permanent.
The unborn, unarisen,
sorrowless, and stainless state:
the cessation of all things subject to suffering.
“The bliss that is the stilling of formations.
This meaning too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The sixth [discourse].
